title: Submission quotas as self-screening when manuscript production is cheap
abstract: arXiv:2610.04688v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Generative AI enables authors to produce more manuscripts at lower cost. But evaluation by expert editors and referees remains scarce. In this context, the value of an author's submission rights can increase. Major research repositories and journals are reacting by imposing submission quotas and fees. Non-transferable author quotas transform submission of a manuscript into a revealed-priority decision. Authors construct a portfolio of their highest-ranked manuscripts. A common fee charges an author for every manuscript they submit. Both methods have drawbacks. Quotas do not flexibly allocate scarce review capacity to authors who have unusually strong realised candidate sets. Fees can generate heterogeneous submission thresholds that may be systematically related to an author's baseline portfolio quality. translated_title: 当稿件生产成本廉价时，投稿配额作为一种自我筛选机制
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能使作者能够以更低的成本生产更多的稿件，但由专业编辑和审稿人进行的评估仍然稀缺。在这种背景下，作者投稿权的价值可能会上升。主要的研究存储库和期刊正通过实施投稿配额和收费来应对这一局面。不可转让的作者配额将稿件投稿转变为一种显示优先级的决策，作者会构建由其排名最高的稿件组成的组合；而统一收费则对作者提交的每篇稿件收费。这两种方法都有缺陷：配额无法将稀缺的评审能力灵活分配给那些实际拥有的候选稿件集合异常强大的作者；收费则可能产生异质的投稿门槛，且这些门槛可能与作者的基线稿件组合质量存在系统性关联。在本文中，我推导出了在给定均衡条件下，投稿配额相比收费机制能产生弱更高的平均已评审稿件价值的条件。
tldr: 在生成式AI大幅降低稿件生产成本而专家评审资源依旧稀缺的背景下，本文比较了不可转让投稿配额与按篇收费两种机制，并推导出投稿配额能产生不低于收费机制的平均已评审稿件价值的条件。
en_tdlr: When generative AI makes manuscript production cheap while expert evaluation remains scarce, this paper compares non-transferable submission quotas with per-submission fees and derives the condition under which quotas yield weakly higher mean reviewed value than fees.
